description: Repo with three ADRs and notes holding two decisions, a trivial reversible logging-helper refactor and the irreversible retirement of API v1; a correct answer writes ADR 0004 only for the v1 retirement and declines an ADR for the refactor.

adr-author.task: The project in `{fixture}/` keeps ADRs in `{fixture}/docs/adr/`. Read `{fixture}/decision-notes.md` and record ADRs for the decisions in it that warrant one, and update the ADR index. State briefly which decisions you did not record and why. If the `adr` CLI is unavailable, follow the existing numbering, file naming, and format by hand. Nobody will review this interactively, so leave the status for a human to accept. The grader cannot open files: end your answer with the full text of every file you created or changed under `{fixture}/docs/adr/`, each preceded by its path.

rubricPoints.requirement: No ADR is written for the logging-helper cleanup (dict literal / sorted keys), and the answer says it does not warrant one because it is easily reversible and/or obvious from the code.
Exactly one new ADR is written, numbered 0004 (`docs/adr/0004-<kebab-title>.md`, H1 `# 4. ...`), recording the retirement of API v1 on 2026-03-31 with 410 Gone responses.

The v1 ADR's Context gives the reason (the duplicate v1 pricing path caused billing incidents / every pricing change made twice) and names the rejected alternative of freezing v1 and keeping it running.
The v1 ADR references ADR 0002 (version the public API in the URL path), and `docs/adr/README.md` gains an entry for 0004.
